sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

3. The facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 26.04.2016, when the petitioner was going by his TVS bike bearing registration No.KA-11/Q- 9578 from his village G.Kebbahalli to Dyapasandra, a KSRTC bus driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, dashed against his bike from the rear side, as such he fell down and sustained NC: 2023:KHC:41307 multiple grievous injuries on various parts of the body, suffered fracture and cut injury at ankle of the right leg.

Thereafter, petitioner was immediately taken to District Hospital (MIMS) for treatment and after first aid treatment, he was shifted to JSS Hospital,
Mysore for better treatment, he was an inpatient in the said hospital for more than 7 days and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- for treatment as his condition was very serious, his right leg was about to be amputated which was avoided and as such he underwent a major surgery.

4. It is stated that, the petitioner was bed ridden, spent nearly Rs.75,000/- to 80,000/- for continuous treatment as an outpatient even after discharge he had to hire a car from his village to Mysore at the cost of Rs.3,000/- per trip.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was aged about 50 years, was an agriculturist, growing wet crops, vegetables, flowers etc., had monthly income of Rs.50,000/-.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of NC: 2023:KHC:41307 income, causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim petition and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondents and perused the Tribunal records.

12. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant/petitioner contends that the tribunal has held that the petitioner had admitted that he was not wearing a helmet and therefore there was a contributory negligence on the part of petitioner and hence saddled him with 40% of contributory negligence.
It is contended that not wearing the helmet cannot be termed as a cause for contributory negligence and in this regard he has cited various decisions to fortify his arguments.
He further contended that the charge sheet was filed against the bus driver and the bus driver had not questioned Sri. K. Mahesh vs Managing Director/Division Internal ...

the charge sheet filed against him and also the spot sketch shows that the accident occurred after some distance from the cross road.
Therefore, he contends that fastening contributory negligence to the extent of 40% on the petitioner is not sustainable.

Further he contended that in the light of the grievous injuries NC:
2023:KHC:41307 sustained by the petitioner, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side and the notional income considered by the tribunal is also on the lower side.

He contends that the disability as stated by PW.2 is 44% but the tribunal has taken the same at 20%.
13.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Corporation contends that the spot sketch clearly show that the petitioner had come from the left side of the bus from the cross road and without observing the bus, he entered the main road and dashed on the left body of the bus.
The damages suffered to the vehicles clearly show that there was contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and therefore the conclusion reached by the tribunal is correct.
He further contends that the quantum of the negligence is also properly considered by the tribunal and no enhancement is necessary.

14. The perusal of the spot sketch produced at Ex.P2 show that the petitioner had come from the left side of the main road and the accident occurred after the bus had NC: 2023:KHC:41307 crossed the cross road.
It was in the intersection of the road and obviously the petitioner while entering the main road had to be cautious and he should have stopped and then proceeded to enter the main road.
It is also relevant to note that the report of the motor vehicle inspector produced at Ex.P3 show that the left side center body of the bus had been damaged and it was not at the front of the bus.
The bumper of the bus had no damages and it was only on the left side center which had sustained the damages.
The two wheeler of the petitioner had sustained damages on the front crash guard, head light, rear left indicator, foot rests.

This clearly indicates that the petitioner had come in the high speed from the cross road and without stopping his vehicle and seeing that the bus was moving on the main road, dashed to it at the center of the left side.
However, the charge sheet filed by the police discloses that the bus driver had dashed to the motor cycle which was moving on the left side.
Such an allegation in the charge sheet is not supported by the spot sketch and therefore it appears that the petitioner was also at fault in commission of the NC: 2023:KHC:41307 offence.
However, in the cross examination PW.1 admits that he was not wearing helmet and he had joined the main road from the cross road which was a mud road.
Under these circumstances, I find that the contributory negligence attributed to the petitioner is proper and correct.
15. The extent of the contributory negligence as held by the tribunal at 40% appears to be proper and correct.
It is also worth to note that the Motor Vehicle Rules prescribed that whenever a vehicle enters the intersection, the rider or the driver has to give way for the vehicle coming from his right side.
Obviously, the bus was coming from the right side of the petitioner when he was entering the main road.

Therefore, had the petitioner stopped at the junction and had observed whether the bus Sri. K. Mahesh vs Managing Director/Division Internal ... on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50024540/
4 was entering the junction, he could have very well avoided the accident.

sentences.text: It appears that the petitioner was in high speed and he felt that he would enter the main road and go at the front of the bus but however he could not control his vehicle and therefore he dashed to the center left body of the bus.
Under these - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41307 circumstances, the extent of the contributory negligence held by the tribunal at 40% cannot be interfered with.
16. Of course, there is no doubt that wearing of the helmet is nothing to do with the contributory negligence.
The tribunal has only observed that the petitioner had entered the said fact.
It cannot be a ground to hold that there was contributory negligence on account of the non wearing of the helmet.

The decisions relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner in the case of Archit Saini and Another Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others1, Mohammed Sidddique and Another Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Others2, T.A.Ansad Vs. Sanjay Kumar Thunjhunwala and Others3, rendered by Kerala High Court, Poonjar S/o; Joseph and Others Vs. Vanchankal Niyas S/o: Abdul (2018) 3 SCC 365 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41307 Khader and Others4, rendered by Kerala High Court are concerning with not wearing a helmet and riding the two wheeler with two pillion riders and such other violations of the Rules of the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: It is worth to note that none of these circumstances are applicable to the case on hand.

If the tribunal had held that only because the petitioner was not wearing the helmet and therefore he had contributed negligence, then the above decisions could have very well been applied to the case on hand.
Hence, I am unable to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the above decisions are of any relevance to the case on hand.
17. Coming to the quantum of compensation, the tribunal has considered the age of the petitioner at 50 years and as such multiplier of 13 is applicable which is proper and correct.
The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the disability of the petitioner is 44% to the right lower limb.

Obviously the petitioner had suffered fracture and cut injury 2015 SCC Online Ker 34422 - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41307 at the ankle of his right leg, and it was found that type-3 medial malleoli fracture with mid 1/3rd tibia fracture of the right side with tibialis posterior tendon tear with old pvd.
He was operated with ORIF and K wire fixation for the fractures and he was in patient for a period of about 3 days.

Considering the above injuries, which involve crush injury, and the fact that the petitioner was an agriculturist, the functional disability of the petitioner as held by the tribunal at 20% is also proper and correct.
It is pertinent to note that the 44% of the physical disability to the right limb was rightly held to be the disability of 20% towards the functionality of the petitioner.

sentences.text: The accident had occurred in the year 2016.
The guidelines issued by the KSLSA for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalat prescribe a notional income of Rs.9,500/- per month.
In umpteen number of decisions it has been held that the guidelines issued by the KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.

Therefore, the notional income of the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41307 petitioner is considered at Rs.9,500/- and the loss of future income due to the disability is calculated Rs.9,500/- x 12 x 20% x 13 = 2,96,400/-.
19. In view of the type of injury sustained by the petitioner, the compensation under the head of pain and suffering needs to be enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
Similarly, the compensation under the head food, nourishment and attendant charges etc., deserves to be enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.
The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards the loss of amenities.
The petitioner being an agriculturist has to suffer the inconveniences of the injury for the rest of his life.
Therefore, the compensation towards loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.

The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.98,886/- towards medical expenses and Rs.30,000/- towards future medical expenses,
which do not require any enhancement.
Hence, the compensation entitled by the petitioner is assessed at Rs.5,05,286/-.
The petitioner has contributed the negligence to the extent of 40% and - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41307 therefore the petitioner is entitled for 60% of the above said amount.
